name: Enoch for Congress
subject: I've heard "just one more chance" before
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Committee to Elect Enoch, Catherine Johnson, Treasurer
body:
I spent years of my life as a counselor, sitting across from people trying to find the strength to walk away from someone who kept letting them down.

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | | Hello Peter,

This week the Vice President of the United States went on a podcast, looked back at the last two years, and made his closing argument to you in six words: _"Give us another chance."_
I want you to sit with that phrase for a second.
I spent years of my life as a counselor, sitting across from people trying to find the strength to walk away from someone who kept letting them down. And I know that phrase. It's the one you hear from the partner who breaks the promise, runs up the bill, disappears when you need them — and then shows up at your door asking you to give them _just one more chance._ Not because anything has changed. Because they need something from you.
That's the pitch now. After two years of rising costs and broken promises, their argument isn't "look at everything we delivered for you." It's "please don't leave us." When the people in charge are reduced to begging you for another chance, they're telling you the truth about their record without meaning to.
And when begging didn't feel like enough, the President reached for the other move: he tried to pay you.
At the Republican convention in Dallas, and again at a rally just this week, Donald Trump promised a $5,000 check to every American — but _only if Republicans win in November._ Let me put that as plainly as I can: the President is dangling a $5,000 payment in front of you in exchange for your vote. There's a word for offering people money to vote a certain way, and it is not "dividend."
Here's the part they're counting on you to forget.
This is not the first check they've promised. Remember the "DOGE dividend" — $5,000 a household, they said? It never came. Remember the $2,000 "tariff rebate" he promised over and over, all last year? It never came either. Every single time, there's a shiny new number and a brand-new promise, and every single time the check gets lost in the mail. By the count of outlets like _Forbes_ , this $5,000 offer is at least the _fourth_ time he's promised Americans a check like this — and not one of them has ever actually been paid.
Beg for another chance. Promise money that never arrives. Repeat. That's the whole strategy.
I'm not writing to make you angry, though I understand if you are. I'm writing because the families of Ohio's 8th District deserve so much better than a party that only remembers we exist when it needs our vote. We deserve leaders who _deliver_ instead of _dangle_ — who fight to bring down the cost of groceries and health care and housing because it's the right thing to do, not because there's an election in eight weeks.
You cannot buy that kind of representation. But you can build it — together, right here.
And that's the honest truth about this campaign: we can't be bought, and we don't have a billionaire's war chest. What we have is each other. [A contribution today — **$25, $50, $100, or whatever you can spare** — is how we answer a $5,000 bribe that will never be sent with something they can't buy at any price: real people showing up for one another.](https://us.list-manage.com/nyzMMsD1yav?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
Will you chip in right now and stand with us?

Thank you — truly — for your time, for your trust, and for believing that our district is worth fighting for. I don't take a single one of you for granted, and I never will.
With gratitude and hope,
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch**

Hillsdale College's popular online course, **" The Genesis Story: Reading Biblical Narratives,"** is now FREE on DVD.

In this six-lecture course, you'll explore some of the major themes of Genesis, including the complex relationship between God and man, and what it reveals about divine and human nature.

"The Genesis Story" is taught by Hillsdale College professor of English Justin Jackson, who has taught the subject to undergraduate students here at the College for 15 years. This course aims to deepen a student's theological understanding of the Old Testament by revealing the literary beauty and complexity of the text.

The course begins with a lecture and introduction by the president of Hillsdale College, Larry P. Arnn, in which he explains why we teach the Book of Genesis at Hillsdale College and why it's important to both faith and higher education.

Then, Dr. Jackson explains the four relationships that dominate the Book of Genesis: God and creation, God and man, man and man, and man and creation.

You'll explore these relationships in the narratives of Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Abraham and Isaac, Jacob and Esau, and finally, Joseph.

This course on DVD is perfect for viewing in your home with your family or for use in small groups such as Bible studies and book clubs.

# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2505%2E135344%2EHFnpYr)
Friends -
We're come up on another FEC fundraising deadline - one of the last of the election - and that means if you're anything like me you're seeing non-stop requests for money from political campaigns and organizations. And as you have likely seen, there are some striking similarities in these emails and the tactics they use:
There's the 3x match!
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-26.79HKre&refcode=em260916&t=2&akid=2505%2E135344%2EHFnpYr)
The 5x match!
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-26.79HKre&refcode=em260916&t=3&akid=2505%2E135344%2EHFnpYr)
And even the 10x match!
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-26.79HKre&refcode=em260916&t=4&akid=2505%2E135344%2EHFnpYr)
Here's the thing: none of that is real. No one is matching donations. They are trying to trick people into donating. It's cynical, and it's something we've never done here.
But we do have very real fundraising goals -- and the money we raise between now and this FEC fundraising deadline will go toward helping me elect Democrats in key races here in Michigan, and in other parts of the country I've been asked to come in and help campaign.
Almost all of the donations we receive to fund that important work comes from people giving smaller donations — often in response to emails like this one. Which means from time to time, as much as I wish I did not have to, I have to ask.
And while I don't expect you to donate to every email we send, I hope that you will contribute to this one. It would mean a lot.
[**With all that in mind, can you please use this link to contribute $3, or whatever you can afford today? There's no matching donation, no super-donor ready to 10x your contribution—but it will help ensure we win a number of important races in Michigan and other parts of the country where candidates believe I can help make a difference for them.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-26.79HKre&refcode=em260916&t=5&akid=2505%2E135344%2EHFnpYr)

On Saturday, the men who built the machine asked permission to slow it down. That is not the same as asking whether we should build it at all.
It is not every day that the three most powerful men in artificial intelligence share a headline, and rarer still when the headline reads like a confession. On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay titled "We Must Pace the Frontier," calling on the industry to slow the development of its most powerful models. Within hours, Elon Musk endorsed the appeal, and Sam Altman reportedly told his OpenAI staff the company was open to slowing down alongside the other labs. For one news cycle, the rivals of the AI race stood in agreement. For the rest of us, it ought to prompt a harder question than the one they asked.

name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Enough of this neurosis
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/911remembrance-12854876?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
King Charles has warned of the "existential dangers" posed by AI. I suppose that makes a change from the time he warned that the "doomsday clock of climate change" was ticking toward midnight. Or from when he told us that genetically modified food risked "the biggest environmental disaster of all time." I do not like to criticize the King of my native country, but I am not sure it is wise for him to keep straying into public policy like this. To be fair, the King is not the only one warning of the dangers of AI. Similar warnings have come from inside the industry itself, from leading figures such as Dario Amodei and Sam Altman. Why, though, would people who have invested billions of dollars in cutting-edge AI want to invite government regulation of innovation in their own industry? Over the past few years, Western AI firms have poured vast sums of capital into building foundational AI technology from scratch. Alarmingly, there is evidence that a number of Chinese AI firms have been able to replicate much of what those companies built. The FBI has described this as "industrial-scale" copying of American intellectual property. Having failed to protect their advantage by technical means, the industry now wants the state to protect it for them. Remember how, a couple of decades ago, we all used Yahoo before Google came along? Imagine if Yahoo had been able to persuade the US government to restrict the development of search engines. What if Yahoo had warned of the risks of "irresponsible" search engines that would allow anyone to look up anything? Some people, they might have said, could even look up how to commit dastardly acts. Regulate it! Or remember when everyone had a BlackBerry, rather than an iPhone? What if BlackBerry had persuaded the US government to slow down the development of smartphones? Those touch-screen devices, they might have warned, would allow all sorts of unsavory social media. Best control it! When AI industry leaders urge the state to regulate their sector, I do not believe they are being altruistic. They are lobbying for a regulatory "moat" to protect their commercial position. If they really wanted to slow down, they could slow down. Among the commentariat, I cannot help noticing that some of the most alarmist voices on AI are the same people who told us Covid was going to kill us all. Cast your mind back to those days of hysteria. Millions of people in countries such as Britain were placed under effective house arrest, needing a reason even to leave their own homes. Transatlantic travel was suspended for months. Schools were shut. Businesses were closed. The real disease was not the virus. It was a form of neurosis: a hysterical overreaction that did far more lasting damage than the virus itself. In the 1970s, the doomers told us that nuclear winter would end humanity. In the 1980s it was acid rain. In the 1990s it was global warming, which during the noughties morphed into climate change. Then came Covid hysteria. Now it is AI. I have no doubt that there will be downsides to AI. Like the printing press, new technology can be put to good purposes and bad ones. The printing press allowed the Bible to be printed and read in many languages. The same technology allowed the publication of Mein Kampf. AI, too, will serve both good and evil. Human ingenuity will require further ingenuity to counter the evil. The risks of AI will need to be tackled — by AI. Just as bad ideas in print were countered by good ideas in print. I am sad to see the King adopt, yet again, such a doomster stance. Think of the history of the English-speaking peoples at times when there really was reason to lack confidence in the future. Think of Charles's forebear, King Alfred, in 878 AD, when Christian England seemed on the brink of extinction. Or in 1315, when there really was an environmental disaster: the crops failed and famine followed. Or imagine what it must have felt like to live in England in 1348, when the Black Death killed four in ten people. You want doomster? Imagine what they felt in November 1916, when the Battle of the Somme ended with some 420,000 British casualties. You want pessimism about the future? Imagine it is London in October 1940. Your city is being bombed to rubble and a Nazi army is massing for invasion. Except that instead of doom, a 14-year-old girl — Princess Elizabeth, the future Queen and Charles's mother — gave a radio address to the nation's children. She assured them that **"in the end all will be well; for God will care for us and give us victory and peace."** Contrast that quiet assertion of faith in the future with King Charles's endless undermining of it. It seems to me that the further we are from real danger, and the more materially assured we become, the more we produce leaders who indulge the ridiculous idea that we are on the brink. In the six years that I have lived in America, I have marveled at the optimism I see all around me, especially here in the South. Yes, everyone faces challenges. The future could go awry. Nothing in this world is certain. Fear and uncertainty are part of the human condition. But here there is an inner faith in the future: that "in the end all will be well." That is perhaps why more Americans, especially in the South, marry younger and have more children than Europeans — the ultimate vote of confidence in the future. The West needs leaders who give us confidence in the future. Leaders who convey the idea that, no matter how great the challenge, we will see it through. Leaders who love our culture, and love those who love it too. Yes, AI will require us to adapt — just as we once had to work out how to make trains and cars safer. But we need to stop this relentless doom-mongering. Enough of this Western neurosis.

clean_body: | | | | | | If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind. | Dear Friend, King Charles has warned of the "existential dangers" posed by AI. I suppose that makes a change from the time he warned that the "doomsday clock of climate change" was ticking toward midnight. Or from when he told us that genetically modified food risked "the biggest environmental disaster of all time." I do not like to criticize the King of my native country, but I am not sure it is wise for him to keep straying into public policy like this. To be fair, the King is not the only one warning of the dangers of AI. Similar warnings have come from inside the industry itself, from leading figures such as Dario Amodei and Sam Altman. Why, though, would people who have invested billions of dollars in cutting-edge AI want to invite government regulation of innovation in their own industry? Over the past few years, Western AI firms have poured vast sums of capital into building foundational AI technology from scratch. Alarmingly, there is evidence that a number of Chinese AI firms have been able to replicate much of what those companies built. The FBI has described this as "industrial-scale" copying of American intellectual property. Having failed to protect their advantage by technical means, the industry now wants the state to protect it for them. Remember how, a couple of decades ago, we all used Yahoo before Google came along? Imagine if Yahoo had been able to persuade the US government to restrict the development of search engines. What if Yahoo had warned of the risks of "irresponsible" search engines that would allow anyone to look up anything? Some people, they might have said, could even look up how to commit dastardly acts. Regulate it! Or remember when everyone had a BlackBerry, rather than an iPhone? What if BlackBerry had persuaded the US government to slow down the development of smartphones? Those touch-screen devices, they might have warned, would allow all sorts of unsavory social media. Best control it! When AI industry leaders urge the state to regulate their sector, I do not believe they are being altruistic. They are lobbying for a regulatory "moat" to protect their commercial position. If they really wanted to slow down, they could slow down. Among the commentariat, I cannot help noticing that some of the most alarmist voices on AI are the same people who told us Covid was going to kill us all. Cast your mind back to those days of hysteria. Millions of people in countries such as Britain were placed under effective house arrest, needing a reason even to leave their own homes. Transatlantic travel was suspended for months. Schools were shut. Businesses were closed. The real disease was not the virus. It was a form of neurosis: a hysterical overreaction that did far more lasting damage than the virus itself. In the 1970s, the doomers told us that nuclear winter would end humanity. In the 1980s it was acid rain. In the 1990s it was global warming, which during the noughties morphed into climate change. Then came Covid hysteria. Now it is AI. I have no doubt that there will be downsides to AI. Like the printing press, new technology can be put to good purposes and bad ones. The printing press allowed the Bible to be printed and read in many languages. The same technology allowed the publication of Mein Kampf. AI, too, will serve both good and evil. Human ingenuity will require further ingenuity to counter the evil. The risks of AI will need to be tackled — by AI. Just as bad ideas in print were countered by good ideas in print. I am sad to see the King adopt, yet again, such a doomster stance. Think of the history of the English-speaking peoples at times when there really was reason to lack confidence in the future. Think of Charles's forebear, King Alfred, in 878 AD, when Christian England seemed on the brink of extinction. Or in 1315, when there really was an environmental disaster: the crops failed and famine followed. Or imagine what it must have felt like to live in England in 1348, when the Black Death killed four in ten people. You want doomster? Imagine what they felt in November 1916, when the Battle of the Somme ended with some 420,000 British casualties. You want pessimism about the future? Imagine it is London in October 1940. Your city is being bombed to rubble and a Nazi army is massing for invasion. Except that instead of doom, a 14-year-old girl — Princess Elizabeth, the future Queen and Charles's mother — gave a radio address to the nation's children. She assured them that "in the end all will be well; for God will care for us and give us victory and peace." Contrast that quiet assertion of faith in the future with King Charles's endless undermining of it. **Fueling the Crisis: How Democrat Tax Hikes Compound the Gas Price Surge
**.Illinois families and small businesses are facing yet another squeeze at the pump, with gas prices surging 21 cents this week. While global conflicts are driving up base fuel costs, the reality is that the Democrats' relentless high-tax agenda is making this cost-of-living crisis significantly worse for everyday residents. In our state, hardworking families are regularly burdened with higher tolls and higher taxes, which only compounds the financial pain when energy markets spike.
.Democrats—like incumbent Sean Casten—pursuing a high-tax agenda makes Illinois increasingly unaffordable. Every time gas and toll taxes increase, the cost of doing business skyrockets, forcing local entrepreneurs to shoulder heavier burdens instead of creating jobs and fostering thriving communities. From job loss to higher prices, everyday Americans are being forced to deplete their savings just to get by.
.In the U.S. House, Niki Conforti will fight to reverse this trend and bring down prices for the 6th District. She will work to cut burdensome regulations in the energy industry to push for "speed to power," making our energy more resilient and affordable. By opposing tax and fee hikes on Illinoisans and curbing the reckless spending in Washington, Niki will ensure that our local families and small businesses can finally get the financial relief they deserve.
Stay informed on this issue—[**read the full breakdown here.**](https://us.list-manage.com/nCreivJPYAo?e=25f4fa3311&c2id=7b058fb5598c3e136d157ed790328086)

I did that math this morning and had to sit with it for a second — because 45 days sounds like plenty of time right up until you break it down.
**Six more weekends.**
**A handful of events.**
**46,000 square miles of Commonwealth, from Erie to Philly, with millions of Pennsylvanians we still have to reach.**
_And_ a far-right opponent whose Mar-a-Lago donors have already written the checks to try and reach them first.
Here's what I've learned running in this Commonwealth, Derek: The campaigns that lose here aren't the ones that get outspent in the final week before Election Day. They're the ones that let a quiet stretch in September turn into a hole they can't dig out of in October.
I've seen it happen. I've watched good candidates run out of runway with weeks to go, not because they did anything wrong in October — _but because of what they didn't raise in September._
That's not going to be us. But I need this team with me for all 45 days — not just the last ten.
[**Here’s the good news, Derek: 45 days is still enough time. Enough time to reach the voters who haven’t made up their minds. Enough time to answer every lie the far-right throws at us. Enough time to win this race and send a clear message that Pennsylvania is not up for grabs. body:
You can bet Mike Johnson and his team are going to be looking at the numbers we put up.
#
Peter —
Republicans are holding on to the House of Representatives by the skin of their teeth. Please, let us explain why that makes your support for VoteVets — at this exact moment — extremely important.
We’re allocating our final budgets as we speak. We’re deciding who we’re targeting, what we’re going to hit them with, and when we’re going to do it. Here’s what it comes down to:
With a majority of just one or two votes, we can put a TON of pressure on the members that have been carrying Trump’s water for the last two years. The people who voted to continue the Iran War, or for Trump’s SAVE Act to restrict voting, or to pass a trillion dollar tax cut for billionaires paid for by Medicaid and food stamps cuts.
The list of vulnerable Republicans is long. We have a ton of targets ahead of us. The GOP knows this, and they’re scared. Terrified, actually. And with the final FEC deadline of the year coming up on September 30th we can have them really shaking in their boots.
You see, after that deadline hits, we’re legally required to report our fundraising numbers to the public. You can bet Mike Johnson and his team are going to be looking at the numbers we put up, because that’s how much we’re going to be able to spend against his members in the home stretch.
If we put out a big number, they’re in trouble. If we don’t, we’re the ones in trouble. That’s why your support, right here, today, is so important.
[**We want them scared. And we’re humbly asking you to make a donation of $5 or anything you can afford to VoteVets to help make that happen.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-sep26.f1bOKp&refcode=em260919-1-180&t=1&akid=35594%2E3013755%2Esiptc4)

body:
The longer we wait, the harder it’ll be to claw back the lead.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1286&source=&t=1&akid=3548%2E124072%2E6EcqSi) | | | |
---
We’re making a risky bet, Peter, so we want to be transparent with supporters like you:
**Roy just approved a new statewide TV ad buy, even though we don’t yet have the money in the budget for it.**
We’ll explain more in a moment, but before we do: [**_Will you chip in $5 right now to help us close the gap and keep our new ads in front of voters across North Carolina?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1286&amount=5&t=8&akid=3548%2E124072%2E6EcqSi)

---
Given that we’ve fallen short of our last two monthly fundraising goals, the timing of this leap of faith isn’t great. However, he had no other choice – because Senate control hinges on this battleground race.
Since far-right super PACs began flooding nearly nine figures worth of attack ads into NC, recent polling has shown our narrow lead eroding – and a brand-new poll out yesterday shows this race is now _within the margin of error._ With President Trump’s personal campaign war chest on its way, Roy’s slim lead could be wiped out entirely if we don’t respond in kind.
The closer we get to Election Day, the harder it’ll be for his message to break through the noise, and for us to continue building the grassroots momentum we need to win.
**Roy gave the green light to invest more now and put our cash flow in the red – but now, he’s counting on people like you to help him close this budget gap.** If enough folks who get why we’re taking this calculated risk and who care about flipping North Carolina chip in today, we’ll be on track to make up the difference and win this race.
[**_Please, Peter: Chip in $5 or whatever you can to Roy Cooper’s campaign today. Every cent will be used immediately to keep our ads on the air so we can fight back and flip North Carolina’s must-win seat blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1286&amount=5&t=10&akid=3548%2E124072%2E6EcqSi)

Fellow Patriot,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let me explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.
---

We ran the most sophisticated ballot-chasing operation the Right has ever put together, and we won every single state where we ran it. 10 for 10. Now we're doing it again, in the three states that decide everything this time. Fellow Patriot, this is how you can help us win this November. **Every dollar you send fuels the machine we're building in Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire right now. More volunteers in the field. Dear Peter,

_" I rang the doorbell, and a lady answered."_

That's how Grace's story starts.

[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=7c1c74ab8b1a44f59b17063f592b5923&_e=OTo4i8Nz7wEQwCoBH7Q8XZaJFBGQDdwkO4Yjr-1e93JYo-ilc5M_CMUWw7uwrAGB8WujyUQdwY8Dlw3CjuXqjkxzQF9CIbJlSiBUZt9tPiFHPPa5GR6roHMUtY91ijA2Y34PX4sDP_d45vxxNoxu4hcDA2RcT-o-tRXQ7Y5B0Zfeb3aZq_kNLMViRhHy-YbxHvzkQf707q91Qlki3eJE8BfVJA2Ig7nXCs6vBM_k9gvbtD_Th7MvvEDZE5ad3FIN6Fq_bhfZ4BUpm38_Xy9Ja_uk5H82yM_mOa5OUslk_w6V_B-c3USveemtvexftlpnyXYA-FpkhuSpWH7oMssxE1Q2BnQeLhhfpK_0QA6cN4SfxMnKtZb1EXIeutICLqD1QLOvEfKWoHZSh8HrhLnb3N7j2NBHwIj3Yz86xL5EO-idhyBNbrYvjmDVmbrZ2-F6R3OdrerRz6aszfJgvYphH2089zPk0SvBeVdRwt906N-a3IixvERQzLY_Qz7V_FH8rnLkZ1oVqMAgbw1PNikL6Q7OJ1tVw_8BROSBMj28hSPkbH391V24jPD1b0Z0xXFjxCOCsGOk9UhYVG6fJhNor9-lIAlXli7-38_1LzzoEwiiD6k-J3GMN8-k56owWnki)

She introduced herself. Told the woman she was volunteering to protect preborn babies. Asked politely if she could count on her vote.

The woman said "no, thank you." Grace said have a good day and turned to leave.

**That 's when someone screamed from inside the house. A second woman ran out the door - she chased Grace down the driveway, shoved her, and hit her in the head with both fists.**

As Grace tried to run away and reached the end of the driveway, the woman threw a dinner roll that hit her in the face - **and kept following her down the street, screaming that she hoped Grace would be run over by a car.**

Grace filed a police report. The woman was arrested and charged.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

Peter, this is just one story from one of Students for Life Action's door-to-door canvassers during the last midterm election.

I've told every one of our canvassers to prepare for anything over the next two months.

I wish I could tell you Grace's story was a one-off. It isn't. Doors get slammed. Voices get raised. Sometimes it gets violent.

And yet our canvassers keep walking up the next driveway because they know if the Abortion Lobby seizes power in November, it will be a death sentence to millions more innocent preborn babies.

**_[Peter, will you please prayerfully consider sending a Care Package to one of our door-to-door canvassers heading into the field this fall](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=7c1c74ab8b1a44f59b17063f592b5923&_e=OTo4i8Nz7wEQwCoBH7Q8XZaJFBGQDdwkO4Yjr-1e93JYo-ilc5M_CMUWw7uwrAGB8WujyUQdwY8Dlw3CjuXqjkxzQF9CIbJlSiBUZt9tPiFHPPa5GR6roHMUtY91ijA2Y34PX4sDP_d45vxxNoxu4hcDA2RcT-o-tRXQ7Y5B0Zfi9G1lu83KYwrZdMEkgcZEk78oJnmXJ_kQq5s-D5Ib1VrZPg-MPjWfDS6mdcydD9-ZVPNBsO5O-Ao-_sBHCVvDXS4GTtnxMiARo2EaMv05ZHji-vmGy0ErU8VmFSXyXtPTxGkRTEjfA4-BAenmQLM-JDFFAgSCLZzThODIoi8Q_BYHMY3Vsl1xCIyhtRBQYY7YLSTTas70P_QlG9V2ZAfkKw81oSe2Oi8562INEgtQqrJg_V0H09O2SNxJIgEYFWfKJ42jsfdj1HuK4XrAXSGi8-Z6OLx5rtwVo5Shbjhg2N-QAJn1ZGIyhRPljPOTqTdTr5ieXU5vedxVtIeqvc7tsXN28GDLUBbtTEx2nt4kexGvjrasf6EaKCOxN0nHlAFPstQ_6QJGFTcPy2i8FBkvn_0q-bSJ8g9KpNq6WR4KtTJtotErAw53vaRl4x2TA4pK-jA_qOjnQmI1kxnlw2MNqa0SC7bNvdjmACUn0G0lpw%3D%3D)_**?

These young women and men will be walking for hours in scorching heat. Knowing pro-lifers like you have their backs will help keep them going.

Of course, I could tell our door-knockers to go home.

I could focus on running expensive TV ads instead.

But studies show that face-to-face conversations move voters more than any TV ad, mailer, or text ever could - and the effect doesn't disappear after one election.

**Voters who talk to one of our students in person are more likely to show up and vote pro-life again in the _next_ election cycle, too.**

_And, it only costs us about $3 for every door we knock._

Not only that, but we'll be deploying teams of pro-life activists to blanket church parking lots with flyers exposing the records of pro-abortion politicians in key districts every Sunday in September and October.

This is the on-the-ground grassroots campaigning that's needed to turn out every pro-life voter.

Last cycle, this approach worked.

***** In Oklahoma,** our student canvassers knocked 633 doors, made 26,931 phone calls, and sent 26,078 texts exposing two pro-abortion senators who killed our Chemical Abortion Pill Trafficking Bill - and voters threw them out.

***** In South Carolina,** we knocked 2,572 doors and made 51,371 calls exposing three pro-abortion Republican senators who protected the _Life at Conception Act 's_ enemies - and they lost too.

***** In North Carolina,** 1,052 doors and 52,554 texts helped four pro-life candidates win their primaries outright.

That's just a small sample of what our door-to-door canvassing team has done over the years. The Abortion Lobby would love nothing more than for our students to stay home this fall.

Right now, we're already deployed and expanding over the next two months, where this election gets decided door by door. Our target map for the 2026 Midterms is the most ambitious we've run:

**> >> Idaho and Missouri** - ballot referendum battles where the Abortion Lobby is trying to buy a win at the ballot box.

**> >> Georgia, Iowa, Michigan, North Carolina, Ohio, Texas** - U.S. Senate races that could decide who controls the chamber.

**> >> Georgia, Iowa, Michigan, Ohio, North Carolina, Pennsylvania** - Gubernatorial and state legislative races that will shape abortion law for years.

**> >> California's 13th, Iowa's 3rd, Michigan's 10th, Pennsylvania's 10th, North Carolina's 1st, Ohio's 9th, and Texas's 34th** - U.S. House battlegrounds where a few thousand doors could flip a seat and determine control of Congress.

We'll be active in at least ten states in races up and down the ballots. And every single one of them needs boots on the ground before Tuesday, November 3rd.

Peter, the Abortion Lobby has the money, the media, and the institutions. What they don't have is thousands of young pro-lifers willing to knock on a stranger's door, get yelled at, sometimes get hit with worse than words - and go knock on the next door anyway.

That grit and determination is what wins elections.

**_[So, will you please prayerfully consider making your most generous contribution to fund our canvassers as they head into the two most important months of this election](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=7c1c74ab8b1a44f59b17063f592b5923&_e=OTo4i8Nz7wEQwCoBH7Q8XZaJFBGQDdwkO4Yjr-1e93JYo-ilc5M_CMUWw7uwrAGB8WujyUQdwY8Dlw3CjuXqjkxzQF9CIbJlSiBUZt9tPiFHPPa5GR6roHMUtY91ijA2Y34PX4sDP_d45vxxNoxu4hcDA2RcT-o-tRXQ7Y5B0ZfR3cyaVyKSNQsTUFsaed6HzvUhUnE4W4UGfwlpzinA_kiz-ABiaR646yss2Hm9WrJA3xGhhmJPiQ6e3BEPwzIzXOAe86MkYSP2QfZrIfpNSN7yGlh4Yb-7A6YKg5qQtHVxA3CYMnUAq6no-gO2_3MDV-UAToHoAr20RYUvcbklQx3GQ_18sDHxTlGnLdu7_gUD_z3hJkrxJ3szzr66l3Vm_MI5km9ZR_PtfYn132g8vOHxTezCIwWA-DX3MZfSMrt3_X_2UpwMkl93wCud-STbjqWvJJ99sDMIxJktr-KGWKR0wOCP8X3Yh4aJde51yIc_rdZE7uGvZokQtNLSh2PXgGB21rEeJjdj_tSUS3RJjCeoccN5aGRzK8I3pGc-qya4HMsRwPo4le9dMu0Hn_Ew_DbwOL72yCJLwxprU85BBY7icHdYOIZ-ODeWdMwMvYgGlbaAWuy2z8zArJ0S9V1t9OTh_B0eS4JsLYkwxAfjkQ%3D%3D)_**?

**> >> $1,200** fully funds FIVE pro-life canvassers for an entire day in the field - roughly 400 doors knocked, one voter conversation at a time.

**> >> $240** fully funds a canvasser's entire day in the field - roughly 80 doors knocked, one voter conversation at a time.

**> >> $70** covers a canvasser's gas for a full weekend of door-knocking.

**> >> $50** puts a canvassing team through a full Church Parking Lot Blitz weekend - flyers, printing, and all.

**> >> $25** pays for a canvasser's meals for a day in the field.

Grace didn't quit after that driveway. And this fall, our students won't quit either.

But they need to know you're behind them.

Kristan Hawkins
President, Students for Life Action

P.S. - Our door-to-door pro-life canvassers will be active in at least ten states this fall, targeting races up and down the ballot. Knowing pro-lifers like you have their back will help them keep going. **_[Will you please chip in $250, $100, $50, $25, or $10 right now to keep our canvassers moving – and protected – all the way through Election Day](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=7c1c74ab8b1a44f59b17063f592b5923&_e=OTo4i8Nz7wEQwCoBH7Q8XZaJFBGQDdwkO4Yjr-1e93JYo-ilc5M_CMUWw7uwrAGB8WujyUQdwY8Dlw3CjuXqjkxzQF9CIbJlSiBUZt9tPiFHPPa5GR6roHMUtY91ijA2Y34PX4sDP_d45vxxNoxu4hcDA2RcT-o-tRXQ7Y5B0ZdF4aS_5T5qxt1XrCuQNHzxXAu0jI9x-Ld0dRloxBnlGZQJpQzS0WACqXSwlEng6mEkCUesihmyIdNVGl8iszB1s2OmNUJIBmOuXCp09ZFFqawLw_vA2qk2yYs4orRCNOG9719iRW3dMwsVBoaNPbAL3t77kqoAlS_nIqSn0helUCF7PuAvxyD35btHK1ideA5fYHLUFzKkUKJ57k9ApDXYevk1QmQuJmBKizkpBmD4YDcR-L3-16KhenkxzmqYQafAiNCuYClbPU1YsBt-ZYRyl-uL__I6f79RSdnnRTxzAQSSu5hZey3l0tbbpv2fSiOz-2JcrjDqTStVPHVgxDtb_V-EaWbPAmG380F2WU6EM3fskEW2og70Z3fpJaD4syeInwm4LjF_FVMLH8YZsWFaKrjv5pQbgzhuNiF-zblMdDkChmhn8Mlt7rQvo9n4R0TbeiwtGTn9jAaIpcFcUsit)_**?

name: Team Cooper
subject: What the GOP doesn’t want you to know
body:
Something is happening under the surface in North Carolina
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1382&source=&t=1&akid=3590%2E124072%2E1-RoQQ) | | | |
---
Peter, we're not sending this message to everyone.
We're specifically reaching out to you because, as our team was going through our supporter records, your file stood apart.
You’re one of Roy's best-informed grassroots supporters. You’ve been getting these emails for a while now, and we see you're keeping up with the latest from our campaign. Thank you.

subject: Your vote-by-mail update for MD-03.

body:
https://elfrethformaryland.com/ [https://elfrethformaryland.com/]

Hi friend,

I wanted to make sure you heard the good news on mail-in voting! Earlier this week, the Supreme Court struck down the Trump Administration’s ridiculous Executive Order to restrict mail-in voting that would have resulted in tens of thousands of legally cast ballots not being counted. I joined House Democrats in arguing against the President’s politically motivated attempt to rewrite the rules — and I’m proud to say we won. Marylanders will be able to cast their mail-in ballots with full confidence that their votes will be counted.

This decision is especially timely as mail-in ballots have started going out to Maryland voters starting today . If you requested a mail-in ballot, keep an eye on your mailbox in the coming days. Despite this Administration’s baseless claims, mail-in voting remains a safe, secure, and convenient way to make your voice heard. It’s used by millions of voters nationwide — even our President.

In Congress, I’m working alongside my colleagues to pass the Freedom to Vote Act and the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to protect ballot access nationwide. That’s because I believe my oath to support and defend the Constitution means always fighting to protect ballot access, secure our election infrastructure, and hold bad-actor politicians accountable. So while the Trump Administration tries to rig our election systems in their favor and restrict voter access nationwide, I hope I have made clear that we will not sit on the sidelines.

Defending our democracy against these attacks requires clear-eyed legislative leadership, but we also need to make sure every voter knows their rights before they vote. That process takes resources.

Please pitch in to help us mobilize voters and defend our democratic process. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-Sept2026-FR-SCOTUSVotebyMail?&refcode=E31673-20260919-SCOTUSVotebyMail-SL-VotingRights&amount=15]

If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

DONATE $10 → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-Sept2026-FR-SCOTUSVotebyMail?express_lane=true&refcode=E31673-20260919-SCOTUSVotebyMail-EG-VotingRights&amount=10]

DONATE $25 → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-Sept2026-FR-SCOTUSVotebyMail?express_lane=true&refcode=E31673-20260919-SCOTUSVotebyMail-EG-VotingRights&amount=25]

DONATE $50 → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-Sept2026-FR-SCOTUSVotebyMail?express_lane=true&refcode=E31673-20260919-SCOTUSVotebyMail-EG-VotingRights&amount=50]

OTHER AMOUNT → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-Sept2026-FR-SCOTUSVotebyMail?express_lane=true&refcode=E31673-20260919-SCOTUSVotebyMail-EG-VotingRights&amount=other]

And if you haven’t already, please take a moment to make your voting plan. Marylanders, you can check your registration status or review local voter tools directly through the State Board of Elections Voter Services Portal [https://elections.maryland.gov/] . If you’re looking to vote by mail, it’s not too late to request a mail-in ballot HERE [https://voterservices.elections.maryland.gov/onlinemailinrequest/InstructionsStep1] .

Thank you for standing with us in this fight.

Best,

Sarah Elfreth

Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. She learned her work ethic and tenacity from growing up in a union household and honed her skills of problem-solving and collaborating over six years in the Maryland State Senate. Sarah lives in Annapolis with her fiancé, Eric, and their dog, Ollie. name: Alex Vindman
subject: What Comes Next Now That the Campaign is Over
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Alex Vindman for Florida
body:
The race is over, and I want to be direct with you - didn't see coming. I'll save the full postmortem for another email. What I want you to know today is that even with the race having ended, we are not going anywhere.
The campaign raised a mighty warchest thanks to donors and supporters like you. With the primary behind us, we're putting this sum to good use by helping elect Democrats in Florida and across the country. Nearly $1,000,000 has gone to Florida campaigns, more than $250,000 has been sent to senate campaigns, and about $400,000 has gone to veteran candidates in and outside of Florida. Over the coming weeks we will deploy more funding to key races to help deliver a blue wave this November.
Additionally, I will look for ways to advocate for policies and advance causes outside of public office. My non-profit organization, the Here Right Matters Foundation, will resume operations with the goal of educating lawmakers and policy professionals on what is needed to defend democracy at home, advance American interests abroad, and rebuild after 2028.
I started this campaign because I believe the fights that mattered - for accountability, the future of America, and reviving the American Dream - don't stop mattering just because an election ended. I'm going to keep writing about them on my Substack with the same directness I tried to bring to the campaign trail about topics like the [**war in Iran.**](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1704?t=1&akid=1128%2E3892029%2E3G6GwR)
[**Please use this link to join me on Substack**](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1705?t=2&akid=1128%2E3892029%2E3G6GwR):
Your support meant... means everything and I can’t do it without you. Please sign up and join me on my Substack.
Thank you.
Alex Vindman

Paid For By Alex Vindman for Florida
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. And with Trump as his inspiration, Tom Tiffany’s playbook is pretty simple: Push Trump’s agenda. Make life as hard as possible for working families. Support billionaire donors instead of Wisconsinites. Meanwhile, Wisconsin pays the price. We cannot afford Tom Tiffany as governor — the consequences would be too drastic. | | We only have 45 days until Election Day, and we’ll be honest: Tom Tiffany and Donald Trump’s extremist agenda is not sustainable for Wisconsin. | | | | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
Hello there, it's Gabby Giffords. Today is Saturday, September 19, and I am humbly asking you to make your first donation to GIFFORDS.

As you know, everything is at stake in the November elections. We cannot sit on the sidelines while Trump and Republicans attack our rights.

So I made a big announcement: GIFFORDS is investing $10 million to defeat the gun lobby’s candidates and win back a gun sense majority.

This is a big deal: Polls are tight, so reaching even 500 or 1,000 voters could mean the difference between winning or losing. But now, I need your help to double-down on our work:

[****Will you make your first online donation to GIFFORDS PAC today? $3 would go a long way in these last weeks, and it adds up quickly when everything is chipping in.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q32026.q0XSG-&refcode=em260919-1-b&t=2&akid=11830%2E3935704%2EMpafb6)

I’m asking, humbly: Please donate today.

Thank you. ❤️
Gabby Giffords |

Peter, I understand the value of a dollar. It’s how I was raised.
And it’s one reason most of my clothes are thrifted. _Really_. I grew up in the Rio Grande Valley where there is some amazing thrifting, and I never grew out of it.

He's handed out over a billion dollars in no-bid contracts to his donors — money that was never his to give away to start with — all while he sits on a $27 billion rainy day fund, refusing to give any of it back to the Texans who actually earned it.
I treat every dollar you donate the same way I treat my own: **Like it matters._Because it does._** And my campaign stretches every dollar as far as it will go.

clean_body: We can't let our guard down. | = Peter, THE GOOD NEWS: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected Donald Trump’s bid to place broad restrictions on mail-in voting for the midterms. Trump’s proposed rules would not only have given him access to states’ unredacted voter rolls — it would have given him unprecedented control over election administration across the country. THE BAD NEWS: The Trump administration isn’t giving up on their voter suppression efforts. MAGA loyalists at the Department of Justice are demanding voter rolls from nearly 30 states, and Trump’s cronies at the FBI have refused to rule out deploying FBI agents to polling places this November — and that’s just the news from this week! The Trump administration is doing everything they can to disrupt the midterms because they know just how unpopular their disastrous agenda is with the American people. | | | | Peter, Over the past year, more than 500 counties and municipalities across America have either heavily restricted or outright banned new data centers. It turns out that when you drain a community's water supply and strain their power grid just to cool down your massive AI server farms, local residents get a little testy. So, what do the tech billionaires do when they get run out of town? They call up Washington and ask to hide their next project on your public lands, where local mayors and city councils can't stop them. **On Friday, the news broke that the Bureau of Land Management is actively considering handing over 17,600 acres of federal land across Arizona, Idaho, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, and Wyoming to build 12 massive new data centers. True to form, they didn't even bother to notify the local leaders in those states.** [**They are trying to turn the American West into Silicon Valley's personal taxpayer-subsidized cooling system. Will you pitch in $10 today to our rapid-response war chest to help us stop them?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/QGUxYpdKAvL5TRKOGnaaAw~~/AAUS1hA~/uT_SIm4ym6ap6C4ei10QofAqO3JtpwHJqArWSZLz_RJrkHY7Ab8xfNZzNbghuEwzdwVW37c7TUOsrriIR0PDFHkRBnrmDnuE37PrHuKOFb3S9W4nMUCF5ehQVo-dpthBBVSBjbdGjul8poFTHT9rLLYOfB1IGGYMNc_E3LgK72mUrBKVLKpqCBQc6JNtGFES6GW1oSClQr4walFiJ4fJ0PHoct3U0D7MkwCRU17iPX70oGhYIS-lPpFUSFEmugWM) The BLM is actually trying to claim with a straight face that turning pristine public land into a concrete industrial complex will "improve electrical reliability." These facilities require so much energy that they are forcing old coal and gas plants to stay online just to keep the servers humming. They are offshore tax shelters masquerading as innovation, and they are using our national heritage as their clearance aisle. Data centers are politically toxic. The vast majority of Americans—regardless of whether they vote red, blue, or independent—fiercely oppose handing over public lands for private AI facilities. True to form, they didn't even bother to notify the local leaders in those states. The BLM is actually trying to claim with a straight face that turning pristine public land into a concrete industrial complex will "improve electrical reliability." These facilities require so much energy that they are forcing old coal and gas plants to stay online just to keep the servers humming. **I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents.**

I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home.

I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country.

After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents.

Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser.

I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first.

Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors.

**I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country.**

Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump?

For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening.

But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question:

Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous?

In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public.

I was terrified.

I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence.

But silence costs more.

So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat.

Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue.

I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first.

Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences.

**That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild.**

Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him.

They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts.

It MUST reach the ballot box.

It MUST be organized.

And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power.

[**So, I'm asking personally: Will you donate $10, $25 or whatever you can afford today to help Resist Reclaim Rebuild defeat MAGA in the battleground races that matter most?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139537928/647683154/-323302678?refcode=260919_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDdkOTYwNWEtM2JiNC1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=MZrEyBXhffdHY8fDfsNeB_C5yCM-CBup46QoaChoiWg=)[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139537929/647683155/949025562?refcode=260919_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDdkOTYwNWEtM2JiNC1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=MZrEyBXhffdHY8fDfsNeB_C5yCM-CBup46QoaChoiWg=)

clean_body: Then I went public.| | | | = I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents. I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home. I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country. After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents. Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser. I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first. Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors. I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country. Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump? For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening. But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question: Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous? In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public. I was terrified. I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence. But silence costs more. So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat. Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue. I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first. Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences. That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild. Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him. They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts. It MUST reach the ballot box. It MUST be organized. And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power. = | | | = MAGA wants us exhausted. They want every new outrage to make us feel a little more powerless. They want us to believe that one person speaking out, casting a ballot or making a contribution cannot possibly change anything. I learned the opposite. I learned that courage is contagious. Control of Congress could come down to only a handful of seats. Your contribution can help elect Democrats who will defend our Constitution, demand accountability and finally place a meaningful check on Trump’s unfettered power. Please help Resist Reclaim Rebuild fight for those victories today. = Stay informed. Stay compassionate. Stay hopeful. But above all, refuse to be silent. **🌱 Peter Hubbard — Georgia Public Service Commission.** Peter was elected to the Public Service Commission in November 2025 after flipping this seat in a special election. He brings years of undeniable experience in Georgia’s energy sector. Peter previously worked as a solar developer and founded the Georgia Center for Energy Solutions, a nonprofit focused on clean energy and lowering power bills for Georgians. His focus is straightforward: **lower costs for Georgia families while building a more affordable, reliable, and sustainable energy system. And he’s not shying away from the costs data centers are putting on residential customers.**

**🌱 Shelia Edwards — Georgia Public Service Commission** Shelia has built a reputation as a results-driven public servant and advocate for Georgia families and businesses. She’s running to stop endless utility rate hikes, protect consumers, and hold utility monopolies accountable. I founded the Georgia Campaign for Adolescent Power and Potential and the Jane Fonda Center for Adolescent Reproductive Health, and along the way, I came to know and love so many people across the state. So trust me when I say that I have a special place in my heart for Georgia. And so do two extraordinary climate champions running to flip Georgia’s Public Service Commission (PSC): Peter Hubbard and Shelia Edwards. You may not have heard of the Public Service Commission, but this little-known board makes enormously important decisions about Georgia’s energy future, including utility costs and whether families continue footing the bill for the massive expansion of data centers. = | = 🌱 Peter Hubbard — Georgia Public Service Commission. Peter was elected to the Public Service Commission in November 2025 after flipping this seat in a special election. He brings years of undeniable experience in Georgia’s energy sector. Peter previously worked as a solar developer and founded the Georgia Center for Energy Solutions, a nonprofit focused on clean energy and lowering power bills for Georgians. His focus is straightforward: lower costs for Georgia families while building a more affordable, reliable, and sustainable energy system. And he’s not shying away from the costs data centers are putting on residential customers. 🌱 Shelia Edwards — Georgia Public Service Commission Shelia has built a reputation as a results-driven public servant and advocate for Georgia families and businesses. She’s running to stop endless utility rate hikes, protect consumers, and hold utility monopolies accountable. Democrats currently hold two of the Commission’s five seats. If Shelia flips this seat and Peter wins reelection, Democrats would hold a 3-2 majority on the PSC, giving them control of this powerful commission for the first time in decades. September 19, 2026
Recent polls by Sacred Heart and Quinnipiac colleges state that Governor Ned Lamont has a comfortable double-digit lead over Republican nominee Ryan Fazio. But it is unlikely these polls are accurate.

Why?
Because Governor Lamont and his handlers don't believe them. Otherwise, they would not be running attack ads accusing Ryan Fazio of supporting ICE and being Donald Trump's handmaiden. The internal polls conducted by the Lamont campaign - which are much more accurate that the liberal push polls from Sacred Heart and Quinnipiac - must show a much tighter race.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1cbd1c94-c3fc-49ad-8a03-fd1ab5aab069?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

Connecticut Gubernatorial Nominee Ryan Fazio

Unfortunately, Fazio thus far is running a typical Connecticut Republican campaign that concedes that since the race is unwinnable, he may as well be pleasant about it. His ads are either feel- good ads or make silly statements that he is going to reduce property taxes. Connecticut voters may be liberal, but they are not stupid. Property taxes are determined by elected town officials, not the Governor.

But Fazio should not just throw in the towel as he is presently doing. He has enough cash - he received $18,000,000 from Connecticut's generous public financing program - to run aggressive attack ads against Lamont on the following issues:

**1\. The Death of Liam Rivera**. Liam Rivera was a two-year old from Stamford who was had his head bashed in and his body stuffed in a plastic bag by an illegal immigrant, Ismalej-Gomez, because this illegal was not turned over to ICE for deportation but was released to the community after he had previously broken Liam Rivera's arm.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/881b9974-5cba-4014-8037-b7061998031a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Liam Rivera who was killed by an illegal immigrant the Lamont adminstration released

Why is this poor child dead? Because of Lamont's policies. And while he is at it, Fazio should point out the hectamillionaire Lamont's only contact with illegal immigrants is when they are wearing leaf blowers in Lamont's tony Greenwich neighborhood.

**2\. Forcing "affordable" housing on towns. **The Lamont administration is forcing towns to build unwanted apartment complexes. Even liberal Democrats in my hometown of Fairfield are irritated about this. Fazio needs to run ads that say if Lamont wins, expect more of this. And then a few years, expect for the taxpayers to bail out the developers when they complain they can't rent out the apartments unless the renters are subsidized by the taxpayers.

**3\. Allowing boys pretending to be girls to participate in women 's sports.** The Lamont administration is [pushing to allow trans females](https://substack.com/redirect/95856c10-bc8e-4146-8d7d-0c66528b77fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (males with XY chromosomes who believe they are female) to compete is women's sports. If this is allowed, women's sports will be destroyed in Connecticut in five to ten years. Presently, three Connecticut high school girls [are suing](https://substack.com/redirect/a46d3f2d-8385-44c8-a1e9-3ebdea620195?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to prevent this.

**4\. Corruption.** Lamont and the Democrats have made corruption an art form. Ballot stuffing and no-bid contracts are only the beginning. Connecticut is not called Corrupticut for nothing.
Lamont recently allocated $250,000 to pay the political hack Miguel Cardona to chair the useless Connecticut Career Pathway Commission.

Lamont and his feckless Attorney General William Tong [looked the other way while](https://substack.com/redirect/aa21518a-30c0-4176-9e85-0f1a56e875b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) State Deputy Budget Direct Kosta Diamantis shook down contractors for kickbacks in order to get state contracts. When federal charges resulted in Diamantis being convicted on twenty-one charges, he fled to Greece. Now he is asking the Connecticut taxpayers [to send a monthly $6618 pension check](https://substack.com/redirect/45f9ea2c-8492-4476-b103-bfe9f9300088?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Greece while Tong is "reviewing the situation." You can't make this up! Tong will somehow figure out how to send him the check while denying knowledge of his whereabouts (Okay. I made this up, but it will not surprise me if this happens.)

These are not 50-50 issues. Seventy percent of Connecticut residents would agree with Fazio if he pushed the above issues.

Fazio probably knows this but is afraid to mention them in aggressive ads because he knows the full weight of the Lamont campaign and the liberal media will come down on him. But if that is the case, he should not have run for Governor. Connecticut has among the highest taxes and slowest job growth in the country thanks to the Democrats. Fazio is our nominee. He may still lose if he fights aggressively. But at least he would go down swinging, not go down groveling.

Last week in North Carolina, our coordinated campaign hosted another successful weekend of action just 50 days out from the election -- and I think the numbers speak for themselves.
We knocked on more than 37,000 doors across nearly every county last weekend alone. For those that weren't able to join us in person, we also made 25,000 calls.
**Between doors and dials, we contacted more than 60,000 voters last weekend.**
That's on top of the nearly 15,000 volunteers who have spent time throughout this race talking to folks all across the state.
Volunteers across the state
Our grassroots team is powered by people who believe in this state and are willing to put in the work to flip seats all over NC. They're working hard every day until Election Day, and we need to keep this momentum going every single weekend between now and November.
[Whether you can join us for an in-person canvass, hop on a phone bank or talk to your friends and families about why this race matters -- every effort counts.](https://substack.com/redirect/aa016412-7407-474e-8f0c-010472796bc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We've got 45 days until Election Day. Let's go!
Abby, Coordinated Campaign Director for the North Carolina Democratic Party

Team,
Yesterday I woke up to the most exciting news of this entire election cycle: **A new poll has us FOUR points AHEAD of Greg Abbott.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a45af9ba-55d4-4b74-b1aa-63a34eefd77d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**[Will you help me capitalize on this momentum by chipping in $5 or whatever you can today so we can keep gaining ground?](https://substack.com/redirect/a45af9ba-55d4-4b74-b1aa-63a34eefd77d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Since launching my campaign against Greg Abbott, I've made it clear who I am fighting for -- the hardworking people of Texas who are getting left behind while Abbott's donors skip to the front of the line.
We have to ask ourselves, is this the Texas that is by and for the people? Or is this just the billionaires' world and the rest of us are living in it? The news of yesterday's poll feels like an answer to that question. Texas belongs to all of us, not just the ultra-wealthy, and we are willing to fight for it.
I am running because I still believe in the American Dream. We should have well-funded neighborhood schools with the best teachers. We should have access to healthcare that we can afford. We should be able to buy a home and not worry about being priced out of it by high taxes and electricity costs. And we should have a right to own land and clean drinking water and not allow that to be disrupted by data centers and corporate interests.
Thank you for believing in me and my vision for the future of Texas. Texans are ready for change and after November, we will have it, but only if we keep fighting.
I'm still connecting with voters, knocking on doors and making phone calls, to make sure our message doesn't get drowned out by Abbott's millions in the nearly four weeks we have before early voting starts. This moment is an opportunity for us to reach even more voters and gain more ground.
**If you 'd like to help us build on the momentum, please [chip in](https://substack.com/redirect/a45af9ba-55d4-4b74-b1aa-63a34eefd77d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) whatever you can today or donate some of your time through one of our [volunteer opportunities](https://substack.com/redirect/cc090570-0e3d-499c-bf32-f73e66059c1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and help amplify our message in your community.**
I am so grateful for the groundswell of support from each and every one of you. We have built this campaign together. Don't let anyone tell you that we can't win because this poll proves that we very well can.
Let's win this!
Gina

| | Peter,
Kansas families know how to live within a budget, and government should be expected to do the same.
As Senate President, I've worked to deliver billions of dollars in tax relief, lowering income taxes, providing property tax relief, eliminating unnecessary taxes, and helping families, seniors, farmers, and small businesses keep more of what they earn.
We've shown that Kansas can responsibly fund our priorities without constantly asking taxpayers for more.
However, there's still more work to do. Property taxes are still too high, families are feeling the pressure of rising costs, and government must continue looking for ways to become more efficient.
I'll keep fighting to cut taxes, rein in spending, and put Kansas taxpayers first every single day.
---
| |
---
| |
---
On the Trail with Ty
---
| | I enjoyed spending time at Johnson County Community College and seeing firsthand the incredible trade programs they're offering to prepare students for good-paying careers right here in Kansas.
Building a strong Kansas workforce starts with giving people the skills they need to succeed and giving our businesses access to the trained workers they need to grow.
Thank you to everyone at JCCC for the tour and for the work you're doing to train the next generation of Kansas workers.

| The Field Report
---
| At the State Fair, Kansans got a pretty clear look at the choice in this race.
Cindy Holscher tried to run away from her radical record. I've spent my time fighting to lower taxes, protect taxpayers, and make Kansas a place where families and businesses can afford to stay and grow. Cindy has spent years opposing property tax relief, and now she wants Kansans to believe she's the candidate for affordability.
This race comes down to where we want Kansas to go next. I'm focused on making our state more affordable, creating better opportunities, and building a Kansas where our kids and grandkids want to stay, raise their families, and build their futures.
I know which future I'm fighting for.

It's Elaine Luria, and Raja said I could reach out.

On November 8th, 2022, after a difficult, expensive, and hard-fought reelection campaign, I called my opponent to offer my concession and congratulations.
It wasn't a pleasant call to make. But I've never second-guessed the decisions that led me there.
If we haven't met: I entered the Naval Academy at 17 and spent 20 years in the Navy as a nuclear engineer, my entire career aboard combatant ships.
In 2018, I ran for Congress and flipped Virginia's 2nd District.
I'm also a mom, which is still the best job I've ever had.
In Congress, I served on the January 6th Committee, knowing full well it could cost me my seat. That cycle, outside far-right groups spent $6,059,677 against me. Add a national environment that was brutal for frontline Democrats, and I came up short.
_**For me, the worst outcome isn’t losing a fight. It’s going down with no fight at all.**_
So I'm back, running to win this seat back from Jen Kiggans, because I can't sit on the sidelines and watch our country descend into chaos.
The Cook Political Report rates VA-02 a Toss-Up. This is one of Democrats’ best pickup opportunities in the country.
Republicans know it too. Jen Kiggans called Elon Musk's DOGE cuts "so necessary," even as they hit Hampton Roads hard. Now Musk's super PAC has started spending to keep her in office and beat me.
That's why September 30th matters. It's my last end-of-quarter FEC deadline before Election Day, and the report that follows is public. Reporters, national groups, and Kiggans' allies will all read it to decide how seriously to take this race.

body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=3240%2E251025%2EWG9CmO ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=3240%2E251025%2EWG9CmO ]Abdul for US Senate

[ Virtual ]Virtual Launch with Senator Bernie Sanders and Abdul on Sept 23 6:15 PM

Abdul and Bernie know that if young people show up to the polls, we will
change American politics forever. Tell every student you know to [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1676?t=1004&akid=3240%2E251025%2EWG9CmO ]join
their call to launch Students for Abdul on September 23rd at 6:15 pm and
learn exactly how we’ll accomplish our goal of RECORD STUDENT TURNOUT this
election.

We know that young voters overwhelmingly support Abdul and his long-term
vision for an America that works for the youth of today. We also know that
voters aged 18-24 have the most underwhelming turnout. That’s what we’re
organizing to change.

Making sure young voters you know have a plan to vote is one of the most
impactful things you can do to get Abdul elected. In Michigan, Senate
races are decided by 1% or less. That means just a slightly higher youth
turnout will mean a victory for our future.

But we’re going for a record increase in turnout.

The difference couldn’t be clearer. Mike Dodgers will continue putting us
deeper into the $40 trillion dollars of debt to fund endless wars that
drive up inflation, and refuse to hold corporations accountable for
hoarding housing. Meanwhile, Abdul will keep money here to fund schools,
affordable housing, lower gas prices, protect reproductive rights, and
bring real, sustainable climate policy.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1676?t=1005&akid=3240%2E251025%2EWG9CmO ][IMG]

This isn’t an election young people can afford to skip out on. The future
of Michigan, and American politics depends on you and me making sure our
friends vote Peter.

Register for our call using this link:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1676?t=1006&akid=3240%2E251025%2EWG9CmO ]https://a4-m.org/s4aLaunch

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1676?t=1007&akid=3240%2E251025%2EWG9CmO ]CALL WITTH BERNIE & ABDUL

See you Wednesday,
Students for Abdul

Will you donate to In This Together PAC right now to support good people running in tough territory?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139540663/647693839/330496673?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_FR_EarlyVote_260919_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTU5N2RmMTYtNDFiNC1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=X7Kwox3nOsru9_8nNQ1lMquPPXlpj802jhALTzz-Bkw=)

I've been traveling the country ahead of the midterms, supporting commonsense candidates running in places that have been written off for Democrats. Candidates like Rob Sand in Iowa, Aaron Ford in Nevada and Zach Dembo in Kentucky’s 6th Congressional District, who are expanding the map and running to deliver real results for their communities.

We have a ton of ground to make up before midnight, and we can’t get there without you. = | | = Here’s why I’m so worried: 1\. Republicans are outspending us nearly 3 to 1. Right-wing billionaires Peter Thiel and Elon Musk have poured millions of their own money into Ohio to try to buy this seat for Jon Husted and protect a system rigged for their benefit. 2\. Our ad payment is due at midnight – and we’re about to fall short. This close to Election Day, it would be disastrous to let Husted and the GOP’s dark-money super PACs dominate the airwaves. 3\. If we lose in Ohio, Democrats lose the Senate. Ohio will be the 51st seat. We simply can’t take control of the Senate if we don’t get our budget back on track right now. That’s why I need your help. I don’t want to have to tell Sherrod we missed an ad payment. You know as well as I do that with under 50 days until Election Day, pulling our ads means we won’t be able to reach undecided voters. = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = Thanks. Lexie Team Sherrod | | Note: This email only reflects donations made online with this email address. If you've made a previous contribution via check or with a different email address/phone number, you may not see it here – but know that Sherrod and our entire team are deeply grateful for your support. = Hey there! It's Sherrod Brown. There's nobody fighting for Ohioans in the U.S. Senate right now, and I won't sit on the sidelines while working people get screwed over by large corporations and wealthy political donors. If you work hard, you should be able to afford a decent life. But the reality is, life is too expensive. Costs are going up. Wages are staying stagnant. Working people are working harder than ever before, and they're not getting their share of the profit. This campaign is all about changing that – and election analysts say we have a strong shot at winning in November. But I'll need your help to pull it off: My opponent is a Washington insider being propped up by the Republican establishment, and he's got virtually unlimited resources. That's not how our campaign works.
